This publication is part of WHO’s recommendations on non-clinical interventions to reduce unnecessary cesarean sections. The recommendations include various interventions categorized as follows: 1. Educational Interventions: Education of health professionals (10 studies) Education of pregnant women (9 studies) Education of the community (2 studies) 2. Management of Labor Interventions: Continuous support during labor (22 studies) Implementation of intrapartum care guidelines (21 studies) Active management of labor (15 studies) Specific physical ambiance during labor/delivery (5 studies) Systematic X-ray pelvimetry in women with previous cesarean sections (1 study) Non-pharmacological pain relief (1 study) Use of computer-generated partograms (1 study) 3. Regulatory/Administrative Interventions: Audit and feedback (16 studies) Peer review (10 studies) Goal setting for cesarean rates (4 studies) Mandatory second opinion for cesarean indications (3 studies) Financial incentives (2 studies) Public dissemination of cesarean rates (2 studies) 24-hour in-house physician coverage (1 study) Use of opinion leaders to encourage guideline adherence (1 study) 4. Other Interventions: Midwife-led continuity-of-care models (15 studies) Exercise during pregnancy (6 studies) Hospital quality improvement programs (4 studies) These recommendations aim to reduce unnecessary cesarean sections through evidence-based strategies.
